title: Nightwatch timetable, variant synthesis, and release notes (draft)
content:
Context:
This is a compact field guide for the upcoming service release (canary -> regional ramp -> global) focused on the nightwatch window and variant orchestration. It pairs a minute-level timetable for the 72h rollout window, a short variant synthesis checklist (mapping model/runtime/quantization variants to traffic lanes), and a draft release-notes skeleton for product + ops consumption. Use this as the single source for on-call handoffs and postmortem notes during the ramp.

High-level objectives:
- Smooth canary with strong early signals so we can aggressively ramp without increased manual intervention.
- Validate variant fallbacks (quantized vs fp16 vs smaller-model) under realistic traffic shapes.
- Keep rollback simple: 2-click re-route to stable model variant + throttle to 25% if a major signal triggers.

Preflight checklist (24–6h before cut):
[ ] Confirm deploy artifact checksum and signed release tag present in registry (owner: release-engineer).
[ ] Smoke tests green in pre-prod and staging (owner: qa-lead).
[ ] Canary config prepared: canary-slice (1%), canary-duration (30m), telemetry-sample-rate 100% (owner: traffic).
[ ] Variant mapping table published and linked in ticket (owner: release-engineer).
[ ] Pager and Slack rota populated for 72h watch (owner: ops-lead).
[ ] Runbook copy of this doc pinned to #release-watchers and included in the release calendar invite (owner: release-owner).
[ ] Emergency rollback script sanity-checked (owner: sre).

Variant synthesis checklist (compact):
- Primary model: redwood-v2-13b-fp16 (latency baseline).
- Fallback 1: redwood-v2-6b-int8 (cost-optimized fallback, higher tokenization variance).
- Fallback 2: redwood-v2-13b-q4 (midpoint, preserves most quality at lower memory).
- Safety / lightweight: redwood-mini-safe (for extremely constrained latency windows).
Mapping rules:
- If latency p95 > 600ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows -> shift 20% traffic to fallback1.
- If error rate (5xx) spikes > 0.5% absolute over baseline -> immediate 50% throttle to stable lane and notify.
- If semantic-quality regression (eval set automated check) fails -> pause rollout and escalate to ML oncall.

Nightwatch 72h timetable (abridged with owners):
Day 0 (T-0 = canary start):
T+00:00 — Canary deploy (1%): deploy complete, verify model health and KV cache priming (owner: deployment).
T+00:05 — Canary smoke (10m): run full smoke suite, run key prompts from regression set (owner: qa).
T+00:35 — Canary review decision: if pass -> proceed to ramp to 10% over 30m. If fail -> rollback to stable (owner: release lead).
T+01:10 — Ramp to 10% complete, check latency, error, cost signals (owner: traffic + observability).
T+03:00 — Ramp to 25% if signals stable for 2h, otherwise hold (owner: release lead).

Night 1 (12–24h):
- 00:00 — Nightwatch handoff: primary oncall gives a 15m walk-through of outstanding items and current signals to nightwatch lead (owner: ops-lead).
- 03:00 — Synthetic traffic spike test (10x short burst) to exercise autoscaling and fallback (owner: sresim).
- 08:00 — Telemetry digest posted to #release-watchers (owner: telemetry).

Day 2 (24–72h):
- +24h — Regional ramp decision: if stable, start region-by-region ramp per the regional cadence doc. If any region shows >10% deviation in cost/latency, hold and triage.
- +48h — Full production ramp target if no regressions. Otherwise, schedule controlled rollback.
- +72h — Final stabilization retro and roll-forward / finalize release notes (owner: product + release).

Signal watchlist (queries to monitor):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (per-route and per-model).
- Errors: 4xx / 5xx by route, model, and region.
- Resource pressure: GPU saturation, OOMs, queue depth.
- Quality: automated eval failure rate on nightly prompt set.
- Cost: tokens per minute and per-request cost deviation.
- User-visible degradation: surge in support tickets or automated feedback (synthetic sentiment).

Immediate mitigation playbook (first 30 minutes):
1) If 5xx spike >0.5% or p95 > 1.5x baseline -> engage throttling: reduce new traffic by 50% (traffic owner).
2) Shift 40% traffic to fallback model variant (routing owner).
3) If degradations persist after 15m -> rollback to previous model + pause ramps (release lead + sre).
4) Inform customer-success for customers with enterprise SLAs and open ticket (cs owner).

Rollback checklist (quick):
[ ] Verify previous stable model tag + artifacts.
[ ] Execute routing rollback script (documented in GITHUB link).
[ ] Validate KV cache flush or warm-up steps for stable lane.
[ ] Confirm telemetry returns to baseline for 15m.
[ ] Post-rollback incident note started.

Draft release notes (skeleton to be copied into product release):
Title: Progressive rollout: improved runtime and routing resilience
Release date: 2028-02-10 (target)
Highlights:
- Improved model routing: more granular fallback tiers and automated fallbacks for latency-sensitive routes.
- New quantization profile: q4-mid preserves quality for long-context prompts at reduced memory cost.
- Telemetry: finer-grained per-model p95 metrics and integrated alerting for semantic regressions.

Deployment details (for ops):
- Canary -> Regional ramp -> Global. Canary slice 1% for 30m, then 10% -> 25% -> region ramps.
- Model variants and routing rules included (link to mapping table).

Known issues (prelim):
- Under high-multitoken concurrency, fallback variant exhibits slightly different stop-token behavior on edge prompts (investigating).
- Small subset of enterprise customers may require a manual pin due to custom tokenization (CS notified).

Post-release retro template (to fill in after +72h):
- What went well? (ops, QA, infra)
- What surprised us? (signals that weren't covered)
- Actions / owners (clear next steps, deadlines)
- Documentation updates needed (runbooks, routing tables)
- Customer impact & communication summary

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize automated semantic regression playbook: who has authority to pause rollouts? (ML oncall vs release lead).
- Complete the per-tenant pin list for customers who must not see fallback variants. (CS + privacy).
- Add a short-run smoke test for tokenization edge-cases to the canary suite.

Appendix (links & quick commands):
- Quick rollback script: github.com/redwood/release-engineering/scripts/rollback.sh
- Canary routing dashboard: dash.redwood.internal/canary-routing
- Observability queries: CONFLUENCE:observability-queries#release-templates
- Slack watch channel: #release-watchers (pin this doc)

Notes to self: keep the nightwatch lead empowered to make the ramp/hold decision without escalating for trivial deviations; we lose momentum otherwise. Keep release notes terse and machine-copyable for changelog generation.

---
End of draft.
